subject: english
title: Compound Sentence Crew Review
objective: Identify two complete ideas joined in a compound sentence.
introduction: Milo joins two ideas about reading and listening. Can you check both complete thoughts and the word that connects them?

vocabulary.definition: a sentence that connects two complete thoughts with a joining word
a word that links two thoughts, such as and, but, or so
words that name who or what and tell an action or state

activities.instruction: Read both sides and notice the joining word.
activities.content: A compound sentence joins two complete ideas with a word such as and, but, or so.

feedback.retry: Find a complete thought on each side before trying again.

activities.prompt: Learn how a compound sentence joins two complete ideas.
activities.narration: A compound sentence joins two complete ideas with and, but, or so. Each side can stand alone.
activities.guideHint: Check for a subject and action on both sides of the joining word.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: A compound sentence joins two complete ideas with and, but, or so. Each side can stand alone.

activities.instruction: Tap compound sentences with two complete ideas.

examples: It rained, so we stayed inside.
I wanted to play, but I had homework.

feedback.retry: Check both sides for a subject and an action.

activities.prompt: Find sentences with a complete thought on each side.
activities.narration: Read each side of and, but, or so separately to see whether it can stand alone.
activities.guideHint: Look for a subject and action on both sides.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Read each side of and, but, or so separately to see whether it can stand alone.

steps: Check the idea on each side

activities.narration: Readers check each complete idea before naming how the joining word connects them.
activities.guideHint: Begin by reading the whole sentence.

items.prompt: Milo writes about reading while a friend listens. Which sentence gives two complete ideas?
items.explanation: I read and Milo listens can each stand alone, and and joins the two complete ideas.

items.prompt: Milo explains that rain caused the children to stay inside. Which choice has complete ideas joined by a word?

options.text: It rained, so we stayed inside.

items.explanation: It rained and we stayed inside each have a subject and action; so joins them and shows a result.

items.prompt: Milo wanted to play, but homework came first. Which sentence tells the whole contrast?

options.text: I wanted to play, but I had homework.

items.explanation: But joins two complete ideas that pull in different directions, showing a contrast.

items.prompt: Ana sings while Ben claps. Which example can stand alone as one compound sentence?
items.explanation: Ana sings and Ben claps are both complete ideas, and and joins them.

items.prompt: Which sentence is complete and clear because both sides are ideas?
items.explanation: Both sides name a subject and action, and and joins them into one clear compound sentence.
